sense: in front, on before the others

terms.gloss: go ahead, go in front, lead the way
terms.grammar: verb, irregular (a compound of eō), with the dative of the person
evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.55: ut singulīs cōnsulibus alternīs mēnsibus līctōrēs praeīrent
terms.comment: Latin puts “ahead” into the verb with prae-: praeīre, go ahead; praecurrere, run ahead; praemittere, send ahead.

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short: the adverb prae is ante-classical)
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 543b–544: Abī prae, Sōsia, jam ego sequar.
Ter. Hec. 371: ūna illārum intereā properē praecucurrit
Plaut. Merc. 223b: quīn ea ego hūc praecucurrī grātiā
Plaut. Amph. 602: ā portū mē praemīsistī domum
Caes. BC 1.39.2: Caesar legiōnēs in Hispāniam praemīserat

phrases.latin: Abī prae, Sōsia, jam ego sequar.
phrases.english: Go on ahead, Sosia; I’ll follow in a moment.

phrases.latin: nam ut dūdum ante lūcem ā portū mē praemīsistī domum
phrases.english: for when you sent me on ahead from the harbour, home, before dawn

sources: Lewis & Short: praeeo · Lewis & Short: prae · Lewis & Short: praecurro · Lewis & Short: praemitto
Plautus, Terence, Cicero and Caesar checked against the Perseus Latin texts; the Amphitruo farewell is also in the Latinitas loci collection (loci-plautus).
